subject: [Notice] EastUS4 maintenance playbook — staggered driver rollforward & customer action items
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@acmeai.com>, infra-ops@acmeai.com
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: [Notice] EastUS4 maintenance playbook — staggered driver rollforward & customer action items

Hi Amanda / Acme infra team,

We’re scheduling a planned, rolling driver/kernel rollforward in the EastUS4 region to address a compatibility regression we observed in a small subset of inference workloads. The goal is to complete the upgrade with minimal customer-visible impact using staggered host rotations, KV-cache preservation, and targeted canaries.

Summary
- Window: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 — 00:30 to 06:30 UTC (staggered across pools; each customer pool gets a ~15–30 min window)
- Impact: expected zero to low latency blips for most workloads; temporary evictions possible for long-running sessions during host swap
- Scope: driver + kernel micro-updates and NIC firmware microcuts on selected host pools

Action items for customers (recommended)
1) Opt-in canaries: If you want early validation, please reply with the pool IDs you want canaried by 2027-06-21 18:00 UTC. We’ll run a small set of canaries and share results.
2) Preserve long-running sessions: If you rely on pinned sessions, add the header X-Redwood-Prefer-NoEvict: true for critical requests; that reduces eviction likelihood but may lengthen host drain time.
3) Test fallback: Ensure your application tolerates 502/503 transient responses and retries with exponential backoff (recommended 250ms initial).

Attachments: redwood_eastus4_maintenance_playbook_v1.pdf (pdf, 860KB) — includes pool map, rollback criteria, and runbook. 
Also attached: canary_instructions.txt — single-page steps for enabling customer canaries.

What we’ll communicate during the window
- Live status updates on: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/EUS4-2027-06-20
- Per-pool completion notifications and rollback notices if thresholds are hit

If you prefer to opt out of the scheduled rotations and request a bespoke maintenance schedule, reply with your preferred window by 2027-06-21 12:00 UTC and we’ll coordinate.

Thanks — we’ll keep this tight.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Site Reliability | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

From: Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@acmeai.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, infra-ops@acmeai.com
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 17:24:00 -0400
Subject: Re: [Notice] EastUS4 maintenance playbook — staggered driver rollforward & customer action items

Thanks Laura — appreciate the heads up. A few quick questions from our side:

- Can you confirm whether the KV cache TTLs reset after a host swap? We have long-lived session data relying on cached prefixes.
- For the opt-in canary: can you run our priority pool (pool-id: acme-prd-34) near the start of the window? We have a release on Wed and prefer early validation.

We may need the opt-out option if the canary indicates any perf regressions. Will confirm pool list by your deadline.

— Amanda
Amanda Lee
Head of Infra Operations | Acme AI
amanda.lee@acmeai.com

On Sun, Jun 20, 2027 at 2:02 PM Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com> wrote:
> [Full notice and playbook attached]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@acmeai.com>, infra-ops@acmeai.com
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Notice] EastUS4 maintenance playbook — staggered driver rollforward & customer action items

Amanda — thanks, good questions. TL;DR: KV cache entries are preserved where possible; when a session migrates we warm the new host’s KV cache using on-disk prefix snapshots and our adaptive warm strategy. There is a small chance of transient misses for very recent prefixes.

Answers
- KV cache: preserved in >98% of host handoffs; we’ll publish pool-level metrics post-window. If you have critically sensitive KV state, flag it and we can schedule a micro-drain instead of a full swap.
- Canaries: we can run acme-prd-34 in the first wave. I’ve added it to the canary list. Expect a targeted 20-min canary run starting at 00:35 UTC in the first pool.

Confirmed items (what we’ll do for Acme)- acme-prd-34: early canary (you’re on the list)- Opt-out window: 2027-06-21 12:00 UTC deadline for requests- Rollback criteria: >1.5x sustained 99th percentile latency increase across production slices OR increase in 5xx >0.7% above baseline for 15 continuous minutes

We’ll post intermediate telemetry snapshots to the status page and DM your infra channel with per-pool notes. If you need us to delay your pool entirely, let us know by the deadline above and we’ll propose an alternate 48-hour window.

Attachments: redwood_eastus4_maintenance_playbook_v1.pdf

Best —
Laura

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: EastUS4 run cadence & escalation readiness (internal only)

Team — quick internal notes (not for customers):

1) Watch windows: first wave 00:30–01:00 UTC (control plane health), second wave 02:00–02:30 UTC (network stack), third wave 03:45–04:15 UTC (driver rollforward). Keep Ops oncall aligned.
2) Canary failure playbook: if canary hits latency/5xx thresholds, halt further waves, trigger JIRA-RT-4821, and escalate to Eng Kernel team (P1) within 10m.
3) Communications: I’ll post per-pool completion to the status link and ping acme DM. Jonas — you own the rollback decision if thresholds are tripped. Grace — coordinate billing credits if a rollback causes >30m customer-visible downtime for any account.

— Laura
